title: Llyr's Shiny Shoes
markdown:
Llyr Bear loved to polish. He polished his little brown boots until they gleamed. Every morning he rubbed and rubbed, and wished he could shine other things too.

Shine, shine, shine — but not all the same.

One sunny day a bright bluebird chirped, “The big show is next week. Everyone must look their best.” Llyr’s heart went thump-thump-thump.

“A big show,” he thought. “I’ll open a special polishing corner.” He put up a sign: Llyr’s Shiny Shoes — Everyone Come.

First, Alfie the pony trotted over. “My feet are dusty for the show,” he neighed. Llyr had never polished pony feet. He tried his usual polish, but it slid off Alfie’s rough hooves. Llyr’s tummy felt a little fluttery.

Shine, shine, shine — but not all the same.

Next, Edie the dormouse scurried in. “Can you make my tiny shoes shine?” she squeaked. The shoes were so small. Llyr’s polishing cloth felt too big and clumsy. He worried he might break them. His tummy felt even wobblier.

Then wise Gran Ada ambled over. “My garden shoes are muddy from the flowers,” she rumbled kindly. Llyr’s brown polish would not work on mud. His knees felt a bit jiggly. The thick mud would not budge.

Llyr stopped polishing his own boots. He took a big, brave breath. Shining was not about making everything the same. It was about making each thing look its most wonderful, just the way it was.

“Alfie,” Llyr said, “I have a soft, fluffy brush. I’ll brush your feet till they shine like smooth stones.” The brush went swish, swish, swish. Alfie’s hooves felt cool and smooth, and shone like river stones.

“Edie,” Llyr whispered, “your shoes are lovely. I’ll use just a little shiny stuff and a soft feather.” The feather went tip-tap, buff-buff. The tiny shoes twinkled like dewdrops.

“Gran Ada,” Llyr said, “we’ll use my strong brush and smooth wax. They will be the best garden shoes at the show.” The strong brush went scrub, scrub, scrub. Then he rubbed them with shiny wax until they gleamed warmly, and smelled a little like a cozy fireplace.

Shine, shine, shine — but not all the same.

Alfie neighed with delight. Edie squeaked with joy. Gran Ada smiled her warmest smile. Llyr’s tummy did happy flips. Each special pair had found its own shine.

That night he set his cloths and brushes in a tidy row. The sign still hung. The moon made a quiet gleam on his own brown boots, and Llyr Bear slept, ready for the show.
characters: Llyr (a boot-polishing bear), Alfie (a dusty-hoofed pony), Edie (a tiny-shoed dormouse)
author: StoryGen Community
